claim: The answers-wave commit widened the closed `input_class` enum to four values in the shipped schema and in ERS-003, but left the owner document's own contracts section stating the three-value closed set, so `Plans/External_Research.md` contradicts itself and the schema it describes. The section also omits the new `declared_source_arm_id` property from the record it enumerates.
evidence: Plans/External_Research.md line 171 (ERS-003): 'A research job admits exactly four input classes: ... and another arm's frozen artifacts admitted as `declared_other_arm_artifact`'. Plans/External_Research.md line 687, section '3. Contracts, Schemas, Events, Or Data Shapes', 'Research job record': 'Required: ... `admitted_inputs[]` (each a `path` plus `sha256` plus `input_class` of `frozen_plans_snapshot|product_brief|arm_artifact`) ... A `frozen_plans_snapshot` input is admissible only on `reconcile` and `compare`; no `admitted_inputs` entry may carry `input_class: decision_record`, which the closed enum forbids outright.' The shipped schema at Plans/external_research_contracts.schema.json $defs.admitted_input now reads '"enum": ["frozen_plans_snapshot", "product_brief", "arm_artifact", "declared_other_arm_artifact"]' with a conditional requiring `declared_source_arm_id` for the new class. The line was true at b56be91761 and false at 0943d85a5a; commit 06535673a1 introduced the contradiction.
suggested_repair: Add `declared_other_arm_artifact` and `declared_source_arm_id` to the Research job record paragraph in section 3 and extend its stage sentence to say the new class is admissible only on `reconcile` and `compare`.

unit: Plans/Glossary.md 'Admitted input class' / Plans/00-plans-index.md External Research row
claim: Two further canonical restatements of the admitted-input vocabulary, both written by this same compile in earlier commits, still name the closed set as three values and were not revisited when the enum was widened, so the Glossary and the plans index now misdescribe the shipped contract.
evidence: Plans/Glossary.md line 209: '**Admitted input class** -- the closed set `frozen_plans_snapshot | product_brief | arm_artifact`. A recorded decision, answered packet or decision sheet has no admissible value ...' Plans/00-plans-index.md line 299: '`Plans/External_Research.md` (`ERS-001`..`ERS-014`) owns external research semantics: the five research stages `discovery | implementation | history | reconcile | compare` and their admitted input classes `frozen_plans_snapshot | product_brief | arm_artifact`, ...'. Both lines are unchanged since the base (git diff --name-only 4f5eda0d18 0943d85a5a lists neither file); the Glossary entry came from 6ca8d64a32 'plans: apply the independent review of goal 3' and the index row from 3c54bede66 'plans: register External Research as the owner of the research capability', both this compile's own work. Both were true at b56be91761 and are false at 0943d85a5a.
suggested_repair: Add the fourth value and its reconcile/compare restriction to both lines in the same commit that widens the enum.

claim: The answers file that authorizes the whole nine-answer wave is cited twenty times by path and SHA-256 as a frozen source, but it is a live file that has been appended to since the reading, so every one of those citations re-hashes differently. The same commit pair fixed exactly this defect for another source (cycle-1 R-10) by annotating the row, and the new citations carry no such annotation.
evidence: Every answer_basis on q-011, q-012, q-013 (ledger 001) and q-005 through q-009 (ledger 002), plus evt-009 on both ledgers and both open_items.json copies, reads: 'recorded in /mnt/Cursor/PM-Experiments/research-audit-native-20260907/process-pilot-20260908/ANSWERS_20260918.md, SHA-256 ec15e8b383322546eed7eb699550b9444b5a27a9d1ab3e8b504adef095a0639c as read on 2026-09-18. Agent-relayed, not verifiable from inside this repository.' That is 18 occurrences across 6 ledger files, plus reports/compile-repair-20260917/verification.json boundary_widened_by.sha256 and one in the bundle README. The file's current SHA-256 is 1f3ba7531118088f61b3d09554d09498e53797bc93ce128f9032c529fa35f3b4; ec15e8b3... is the SHA-256 of its first 2108 bytes, the file as it stood before the two Azure DevOps sections were appended (verified by hashing the prefix ending just before '## Azure DevOps candidates'). By contrast the same cycle-1 fix annotated Plans/Decision_Log.md in the evidence shard as 'a live canon document that changes; ... so a mismatch is expected'.
suggested_repair: Annotate the ANSWERS_20260918.md citations the way the evidence shard's moving-source rows are annotated, or cite a frozen copy of the nine-item section rather than the growing file.

claim: The clause that marks `visible_only` a design default was attached to a four-item list with the referring phrase 'the second of which', whose nearest referent is the per-job limits. On that reading canon says the per-job limits are an unexercised design default, which the next sentence of the same paragraph and ERS-009 both contradict. The marking also reaches only the section prose, not SSYS-037's canonical_text or its acceptance criteria.
evidence: Plans/Settings_System.md SSYS-037 prose: 'Settings owns the four Project-scoped values that bound an external research topic: the per-topic cost cap, the per-job limits on model responses and wall seconds, the lifetime cap per research arm, and whether retained unresolved usage blocks further admission or only stays visible, the second of which is a design default no run has exercised yet.' Fourth sentence of the same paragraph: 'The per-job limits are the live bound in practice ...'; ERS-009 canonical_text: 'In continuation 4 of the Jujutsu research they ended 33 of 80 jobs, 47 finished'. SSYS-037's canonical_text still reads only 'an unresolved-usage disposition of blocks_admission or visible_only' with no design-default marking, and no acceptance criterion carries one. ERS-009, by contrast, carries the marking in canonical_text: '`visible_only` is a design default that no run has exercised yet, and it stays marked as one until a run does.'
suggested_repair: Replace 'the second of which' with a phrase that names `visible_only`, and carry the marking into SSYS-037's canonical_text as ERS-009 does.

claim: The new obligation that `visible_only` 'stays marked as one until a run does' is stated only in canonical_text: no acceptance criterion tests it, no negative constraint forbids presenting it as exercised, and unlike the three obligations this compile does track, it is not recorded as an open question, so nothing fails when it is violated.
evidence: ERS-009 canonical_text: 'The blocking branch is what continuation 4 exercised; `visible_only` is a design default that no run has exercised yet, and it stays marked as one until a run does.' Its four acceptance criteria are unchanged and none mentions the disposition's provenance; its three negative_constraints are unchanged. Ledger 001's own standard for this case, state/current.json validation_state.partial_enforcement: 'Three obligations have no validator surface and are recorded as open questions q-008, q-009 and q-010 rather than implied by the contracts.' Ledger 002 records q-007 as answered and closed.
suggested_repair: Add a criterion that a research limits surface presenting `visible_only` names it a design default until a run establishes it, or keep q-007 open as an unenforced obligation.

evidence: Plans/Jujutsu_Integration.md line 347: 'preserved_exact_tokens: [Install Jujutsu, Use Jujutsu here, Bookmarks, Operation Log, Ready with limits, Needs attention, native_toolchain_identity, toolchain_identity, certified_scenarios, ...]'. claim: The new acceptance criterion has two clauses but only one is fixture-proven: one negative fixture proves an undeclared other-arm input is rejected, and none proves that another input class carrying `declared_source_arm_id` is rejected, although the schema's else branch encodes it.
evidence: ERS-003 criterion: 'A `declared_other_arm_artifact` input names the arm it came from in `declared_source_arm_id`, and no other input class carries one; an undeclared other-arm input is rejected before dispatch.' The one new negative, Plans/external_research_contract_fixtures.json 'job_other_arm_artifact_without_a_declaration', patches 'admitted_inputs.3.declared_source_arm_id' to null on the new positive. No negative sets `declared_source_arm_id` on an `arm_artifact`, `product_brief` or `frozen_plans_snapshot` entry. ATS-054's own discipline is '30 negative fixtures each mutating one named positive so that it fails for exactly one named constraint'. Separately, that negative's `rejects_for` names the required check, 'admitted_input.declared_source_arm_id required for declared_other_arm_artifact', while a null value actually fails the non_empty_string type in the conditional's then branch.
suggested_repair: Add one negative that sets `declared_source_arm_id` on an `arm_artifact` input, and name the constraint the existing negative actually fails.

claim: The bundle README's section 'What is deliberately not done here' was not revisited by either cycle-2 commit and now presents all eight answered questions as open and deliberately unmade, contradicting the same README's own boundary paragraph, the receipt's open_questions field and the ledgers. Two of its entries state the opposite of what the branch ships. Recorded after reading the bundle, as the brief permits.
evidence: README: 'Eight obligations need an owner decision or a schema change and are recorded as open ledger questions rather than asserted in canon. None blocks landing.' followed by q-011, q-012, q-013, q-005, q-006, q-007, q-008 and q-009. Its q-012 entry reads 'The shared definition is `native_toolchain_identity` and the property that carries it is `toolchain_identity`; canon now names both rather than only the property', after the same branch renamed the property in 17 places. Its q-005 entry reads 'A prose scope qualifier would be enough; a new input class would be a schema change', after the same branch added `declared_other_arm_artifact`. Its q-006 entry reads 'The shard does not name it' after the shard was amended to name it, and its q-009 entry poses the heading question after the three headings were added. verification.json records all eight under 'answered_by_this_branch' and lists a different nine as open; the README's own bullet three paragraphs earlier says 'Jared answered "agree" to all nine recommendations on 2026-09-18'.
suggested_repair: Rewrite that section to say what the nine answers changed and list only the nine questions the receipt records as open.

claim: The README's disposition table was not refreshed when one External Research finding moved from deferred to repaired in the cycle-2 commits, so two of its cells disagree with the dispositions file and with the receipt's own counts. Recorded after reading the bundle.
evidence: README table: External Research column 'confirmed and repaired 32' and 'confirmed, deferred to an open question 11'. Counting reports/compile-repair-20260917/findings-dispositions.jsonl over the four External Research packets gives confirmed_and_repaired 33 and confirmed_deferred_to_question 10. git diff b56be91761 0943d85a5a on that file shows exactly one row changed: er-reviewer-b POSTb-R-05 from confirmed_deferred_to_question to confirmed_and_repaired. verification.json's totals, 93 repaired and 12 deferred over 146 rows, match the file; the README's totals row, 82 and 11 over 134, does not.
suggested_repair: Update the two cells to 33 and 10.
